t.5.6.1: The mighty one beheld that cluster of mansions, hung with lattices of lapis lazuli and gold, like a vast mass of clouds in the rainy season, bound with lightning and filled with flocks of birds.
t.5.6.2: He saw the various halls of the dwellings, the halls for the finest conches, weapons and bows, and also, upon the mountain-like mansions, charming and spacious moon-terraces.
t.5.6.3: The monkey beheld the mansions, resplendent with manifold treasures, well honoured even by gods and asuras, free from every defect, and won by their owners' own might.
t.5.6.4: He saw the mansions of the lord of Laṅkā, built with great care, as if fashioned by Maya himself, surpassing all others on the face of the earth in every excellence.
t.5.6.5: Then he beheld the finest of mansions belonging to the lord of the Rākṣasas, befitting his own might, shaped like a towering cloud, captivating to the mind, lovely with its golden form, and truly of a beauty beyond compare.
t.5.6.6: Like heaven spread out upon the surface of the earth, it blazed with splendor and was strewn with many jewels; covered with the blossoms of many kinds of trees, it looked like a mountain's summit covered with pollen.
t.5.6.7: Glowing as if with the finest of women, honored like a rain-cloud by flashes of lightning, seemingly drawn along by the finest of swans, and endowed with splendor, it was like the aerial chariot of the virtuous in the sky.
t.5.6.8: He beheld that jewel among aerial chariots, brilliant with many gems and adorned with artfully arranged clouds, like a mountain peak streaked with many minerals, like the sky spangled with planets and the moon.
t.5.6.9: The earth was fashioned there, filled with ranges of mountains; the mountains were fashioned filled with canopies of trees; the trees were fashioned filled with canopies of blossoms; and the blossoms were fashioned filled with filaments and petals.
t.5.6.10: There were white mansions that had been built, and likewise lotus ponds full of beautiful flowers, and again lotuses with their filaments, and lovely, variegated groves as well.
t.5.6.11: There the great monkey beheld the great aerial chariot called Puṣpaka, resplendent and ever more brilliant with the radiance of its jewels, and lofty in height even among the finest of mansions.
t.5.6.12: There were birds fashioned of beryl, and likewise birds of silver and coral; serpents made bright with many kinds of gems, and horses of beautiful limbs, true to their noble breed.
t.5.6.13: Birds were fashioned there, fair of face and lovely of wing, their wings wrought of coral, gold and flowers, their curving wings playfully bent; they shone as if they were the very wings of Kāma himself.
t.5.6.14: There were elephants with fine trunks, being set to their task, holding blue lotus petals with their filaments in their trunks; and the goddess Lakṣmī was fashioned with lovely hands, standing likewise upon the lotus and holding a lotus in her hand.
t.5.6.15: Thus, filled with wonder, he approached that splendid house, which shone like a beautifully gleaming mountain, and again beheld that supremely fragrant and lovely dwelling, like a mountain with charming caves at the close of winter.
t.5.6.17: Then the mind of that great-souled one, keen-eyed, self-disciplined, of a mind cultivated in many ways and walking the right path, became deeply distressed as he roamed about without seeing the daughter of Janaka.
t.5.6.16: Then the monkey, having leapt into that honoured city guarded by the arms of the Ten-faced one, roamed through it, yet did not see Janaka's daughter, the greatly revered one, deeply sorrowful and overcome by the force of her husband's virtues.
